question: What steps must I follow to resolve a roommate conflict before a room change can be approved?
answer: To resolve a roommate conflict, you must first speak with your roommate or floormate. If the issue is not resolved, you must speak with your Resident Assistant (RA) for mediation. If a resolution is still not reached, you must then speak with your Residence Life Coordinator (RLC).
quote: For roommate or ﬂoor mate conﬂicts, the process begins by speaking with your roommate or ﬂoor mate. If it cannot be worked out, you must then speak with your Resident Assistant (RA) to facilitate mediation. If resolution is still not made, then you are to speak with your Residence Life Coordinator (RLC).

question: What are the quiet hours on weekdays and weekends, and how do they change during finals?
answer: Quiet hours are from 10:00 pm to 8:00 am Sunday through Thursday, and from 12:00 am to 10:00 am on Friday and Saturday. During finals week, 24-hour quiet hours are enforced starting on the day before the first day of finals.
quote: Quiet Hours: ● Sunday-Thursday 10:00 pm-8:00 am ● Friday & Saturday 12:00 am-10:00 am ● During Finals week there are 24-hour quiet hours that are enforced starting on the day before the ﬁrst day of Finals

question: How long can an overnight guest stay, and whose permission or notification is required?
answer: Overnight guests are permitted to stay for up to three consecutive nights. The host is required to obtain permission from their roommate, get a guest pass from Security, and notify their RA.
quote: Residents may have overnight guests for up to three (3) consecutive nights. As host, you need permission from your roommate, and a guest pass from Security. You also need to notify your RA.

question: Which students must live in college housing and have a dining plan, and what exceptions are listed?
answer: Full-time students are required to live in college housing and subscribe to a dining plan during their first six credit terms. Exceptions to this policy include married students, military veterans with two years of active duty, students with dependent children, and commuting students who live with their parents or legal guardians within a 30-minute commute. Any other exceptions must have prior approval from the Director of Residence Life.
quote: For this reason, full-time students are required to live in College housing and subscribe to a dining plan during their ﬁrst six credit terms. College housing includes residence halls, fraternities, sororities, apartments, special interest houses, and townhouses. Exceptions to this policy include married students, military veterans with two years of active duty, students with dependent children, and commuting students who live with their parents/legal guardians within a 30-minute commute.

question: I locked myself out at 11 p.m. on Saturday. Who should I contact, and would that be different during weekday office hours?
answer: If you are locked out at 11 p.m. on Saturday, you should contact Security. Yes, this would be different during a college work day (weekday office hours), when you should instead call the Residence Life Office.
quote: If it is after oﬃce hours or on the weekend, the student should contact Security, who can let them in.

question: I lost my room key. What steps do I need to take to get a replacement?
answer: To get a replacement for a lost room key, you must contact Residence Life immediately, fill out a key replacement form, and take it to Security so they can cut a new key for your room.
quote: If the student loses their key, they should contact Residence Life immediately, ﬁll out a key replacement form, and take it to Security to have a new key cut for their room.

question: What should I do if I lose my student ID, and is the first replacement free?
answer: If you lose your student ID card, you should report the loss to Residence Life and fill out a lost ID card form. The first replacement card is provided for free.
quote: Students who have lost their ID card/meal card/key card should report it to Residence Life and ﬁll out a lost ID card form. Residence Life will make you a new card for free if it is your ﬁrst time losing it.

question: I paid the guest meal price because I forgot my ID. Can I get a refund?
answer: Yes, you can receive a full refund if you present the receipt and your valid ID at the Food Service Office within 72 hours.
quote: However, the student will be issued a receipt and can receive a refund, in full, if the student presents the receipt and their valid ID at the Food Service Oﬃce within 72 hours.

question: What must I do before parking in a campus Student Parking lot, and what happens if I leave a parking ticket unpaid for more than 30 days?
answer: To park in a campus Student Parking lot, you must purchase a parking permit. If you leave a parking ticket unpaid for more than 30 days, the fine will double and the charge will be added to your student account.
quote: After 30 days, the ﬁne will double and the charge will be added to the student account.

question: I am already living on campus for summer housing or an activity. When must I clear an Accounting/Enrollment hold, and what happens if I do not?
answer: Students who are already living on campus for summer housing or co-curricular activities must clear an Accounting/Enrollment hold at least one week before the first day of classes. If they fail to do so, they will be required to move out of the Residence Halls and will not be permitted to attend classes or participate in co-curricular activities.
quote: Students who are already living in the Residence Halls due to summer housing or co-curricular activities must clear an Accounting/Enrollment hold no later than one week before the first day of classes. Students who do not meet this deadline will be required to move out of the Residence Halls and may not attend classes or participate in co-curricular activities.

question: I earned a D+ in a course. Can I repeat it, and which attempt counts toward my GPA and earned units?
answer: Yes, you can repeat a course if you received a grade of "D+" or lower. The grade and credit from your most recent attempt will be used in calculating your cumulative grade point average and earned unit count.
quote: Students may repeat a course if they received a grade of “D+” or lower. Credit for the grade from the most recent course attempt will be used in calculating the grade point average and earned unit count.

question: Under what circumstances can I receive an incomplete grade?
answer: Incomplete grades are granted only in situations involving serious illness or injury, a family crisis, or other documented, unexpected events outside of the student's control that make finishing course requirements by the end of the semester impossible.
quote: Incomplete grades shall be granted only in cases of serious illness or injury, family crisis, or some other substantiated unforeseen circumstance beyond the control of the student that would make it impossible to complete all course requirements by the end of the semester.

question: How do I drop a course after the first week of classes but before the drop deadline?
answer: To drop a course after the first week of classes but before the relevant drop deadline, you must acquire an Add/Drop Card from the Registrar’s Office located on the second floor of Pearsons Hall. You will need to obtain the written approval of the course instructor(s) and your primary academic advisor on this card, and then submit the completed Add/Drop Card back to the Registrar’s Office for final processing.
quote: A student can drop a course after the first week of classes and before the relevant drop deadline by acquiring an Add/Drop Card from the Registrar’s Office on the second floor of Pearsons Hall.

question: How many earned units do I need to graduate, and what minimum GPA is required overall and in my major?
How many units can a Data Science or Data Analytics major double-count toward another major or minor?
answer: A student majoring in data science or data analytics can double-count up to four units toward another major or minor.
quote: If students majoring in data science or data analytics want to major or minor in another discipline, up to four units are allowed to be double counted.

question: Can AP credit satisfy the writing or quantitative reasoning requirements, and how does that differ from transferring a college course?
answer: AP, IB, and GCE A-level credits cannot be used to satisfy writing or quantitative reasoning requirements, as they are prohibited from fulfilling any domain or skills requirements. Conversely, a transfer course can be used to fulfill the quantitative reasoning requirement, and one out of the three required writing courses can be a transferred course.
quote: Transfer courses may be used to satisfy all 5 domain requirements and two of the five skills requirements, with the following limitations: - One out of the three required writing courses may be a transferred course. - The quantitative reasoning requirement may be fulfilled with a transfer course. - The intercultural literacy requirement must be fulfilled at Beloit College. - AP/IB/GCE A-level credits may not be used to fulfill any of these requirements.

question: I want to take a course at another college to meet Beloit's quantitative reasoning requirement. What should I do before enrolling, and what minimum grade would make it eligible for transfer?
answer: Before enrolling in a course at another college, you should complete the Transfer Credit Authorization Form. Additionally, you must earn a grade of "C" or better for the credit to transfer.
quote: Students enrolled at Beloit who wish to transfer credits for coursework taken after matriculation should complete the Transfer Credit Authorization Form prior to enrolling in a course elsewhere.

question: I missed the normal drop deadline but am still earning a D. Can I request a WP, what documentation is needed, and will I receive credit?
answer: Yes, you can request a "withdraw passing (WP)" if you are passing the course with a "D" or better. To do so, you must provide a written petition containing the course details, semester, and instructor name. Additionally, both your instructor and advisor must provide written statements, with the instructor's statement verifying your passing status of a "D" or better. You will not receive any credit for a course in which a WP is received.
quote: No credit is granted for a course in which a WP is received, but the course appears on the transcript with a grade of “WP”.

Can I bring a pet cat to campus housing, and would calling it an emotional support animal be enough?
answer: Yes, a cat can be kept as an emotional support animal, but simply calling it one is not enough. You must obtain official Emotional Support Animal designation from the Director of Learning Enrichment and Disability Services before bringing the animal to campus, as keeping an animal without authorization is not permitted.
quote: Students must receive Emotional Support Animal designation from the Director of Learning Enrichment and Disability Services (hereto referred to as “Director”) prior to bringing their animal to campus.
